utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Weber, the Chamber was informed that you'd like to put something on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours and good morning. There's just one brief matter I wanted to put on the record with respect to Exhibit D399 currently marked for identification. With respect to this annotated photograph, the Prosecution asked the Defence for the basis of its assertion made to the witness at transcript page 18815, line 3, that the area marked as Colina Kapa in this photo is the position at which OP-1 was situated. The Defence has not provided us with the source of this information. The Prosecution notes at this time that it also checked its evidence, in particular, P1751, and that it does not agree that this annotated photograph accurately depicts the location of OP-1. Thank you, Your Honours for letting me put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, I take it that you will take care of it. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. But before -- yes, please. Have the parties reached an agreement on how to divide the time this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think Mr. Weber asked for one hour, so I will leave that last hour for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's the agreement, then we'll stick to that. Meanwhile, I use the time to deal with a follow-up on Witness RM038. In court, on the 31st of October of this year, the Prosecution indicated that it would inform the Chamber in the week of the 4th of November whether it would maintain its Rule 92 bis application for Witness RM038 that is part of the 28th Rule 92 bis motion. This can be found on transcript pages 18539 and 40, and could the Prosecution advise on its position.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you would allow us to just give you an answer at the next break, we will be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps needless to say but I nevertheless remind you that you're bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P867 in e-court, please. We need page 12 in English and 11 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, this morning, we are probably going to dwell upon -- on the issue of humanitarian aid of the 14th of -- 4th of February, 1994. According to the police report, the explosions took place on a Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street and Mihajlo Pupin number 3, and on the pavement between the playground and the garage. In the report that we see before us, the forensic and anti-sabotage department says that an explosion took place on Dzavarahalal Nehura Street. Did you make any comparison of the data and how come that we have a different address now in this police report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure why there would be a different address. I didn't check the -- the specific numbers or the addresses while looking at the -- the reports I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this location, the Dzavarahalal Nehura Street, is 200 metres away from the location indicated as the point of impact in other reports?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now focus our attention to the incident of 22nd January 1994 in Alipasino Polje. During this incident, according to the reports, three shells fell. The first one landed in the park on Rade Koncar Square; the second in Cetinjska Street 3; and the third one on Klara Cetkin number 4. Is that correct? Is that what the report says?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the report in front of me, and I can't remember if the -- that was mentioned in the reports that I looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have this in document P865 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please slow down when reading the numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited to more slowly read the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Exhibit P865, we are not going to call it up. English page 4; B/C/S page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you established the azimuth or the bearing angle from which the shells arrived?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, when I was able to visit the scene, the deterioration of the craters was such that it was impossible to use them for any way of confirming a direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Due to that, you decided to give your confidence to the forensic CSB Sarajevo team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All I had to go off was the -- the reports I had been given, so I based my report on -- on those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you take into consideration the fact that the CSB findings concerning the shell calibre were contrary to the findings of the forensic technician who conducted the investigation alongside them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the conflict between the forensic investigation and that of, I believe it's a Captain Verdy but I wasn't aware of any other conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay, well, I'll give the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just believe it's not an accurate statement in counsel's just -- previous question on page 4, lines 18 to 20 that the investigation conducted alongside one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's see P865, English page 7 and B/C/S page 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did I hear you say 865?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, we see again a document produced by the forensic and counter-terrorism department. It says under item 4 that on the 22nd January 1994 at around 1320 hours, two mortar shell came from the west, of calibre 120-millimetres, on a Klara Cetkin Street number 4 and the second one hit Cetinjska Street at number 3. So, in addition to Captain Verdy's findings, we have these findings as well. Did you take that into account?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From looking at this report, I can't be certain that this is actually relating to the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] It's the same date; right? It talks about 22nd January 1994.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same date, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it does come under the number we received from the Prosecution in relation of this incident. But I will not dwell on it anymore, since we are a bit tight with the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can ask Ms. Stewart to possibly print out pages 7 to 9 which is the complete report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Weber has the time in his redirect. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If it will assist [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber -- Mr. Weber is offering assistance and you say you don't need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't need it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also compared the ballistics CSB Sarajevo report with the findings of UNPROFOR team - is that correct? - and in the process you mentioned Captain Verdy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please have 65 ter 10570.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this report, Captain Verdy, just like in the previous one we saw, says that on that day three 120-millimetre shells also exploded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this report he refers to three rounds exploding, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that an experienced ballistic expert could easily distinguish between a 120-millimetre shell explosion and that of 82-millimetre explosion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the ground and what it hits, yes, he should be able to tell the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this document into the evidence, Your Honour. If it's not already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could check if it's already been admitted. I think it might be actually under a Defence exhibit number but I can check and get back to you on the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please check and then we will deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D672 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Stewart very quickly checked and she has it admitted as D178. D178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, no need to decide --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on the tendering.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we please have 1D672 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this photograph, one can see the point of impact on Klara Cetkin Street in front of number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just going to -- just my concern with what counsel is continuing with in this photograph is just the foundation: Who took it, when it took, what it depicts. And I'm concerned that counsel is going to be testify as to what it represents, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, where does it come from, when was it taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have this with me right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just proceed on an assumption, and if the assumption turns out to be wrong - and Mr. Lukic you should inform us in more detail about where it is - and then you would have lost time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on since I'm not sure about the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You always can revisit the matter after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you agree to take a look at P865? We need page 8 in English and 15 in B/C/S. You can see in the penultimate paragraph on the screen, this is a record on the forensic investigation of the scene, the artillery projectile that fell on Klara Cetkin and Cetinjska Streets and it says that the star-shaped traces are around 120 centimetres in length. You have visited the scene, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have visited the scene, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that on the spot, the length of these star-shaped traces is actually around 3 metres?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot obviously determine that from just this report and from the previous picture. I am a little confused because, in the same paragraph, it says that the traces of the primary crater are barely visible. But in the previous picture, they were visible. So I'm a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution is just seeking to avoid confusion. We have printed a whole copy of this report, if it would assist. It's a rather dense report. If it would assist the witness in looking at it. And I believe the picture was dropped by Mr. Lukic and wasn't proceeded with. I don't know if that's the same picture that the witness is now thinking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know. If the witness needs to see more of the report, please do not hesitate to ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm going to continue. I have a lot to do today.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel kindly wait for the B/C/S interpretation to finish before continuing to read in B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited to wait for the B/C/S translation to be finished before you go on reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report, you wrote that 82-millimetre shells had been fired from the direction of Nedzarici, westerly direction. On what basis did you reach this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was from the basis of the -- the -- the forensic report. Because of the -- the poor quality of the craters, they could not accurately identify a precise direction, only an approximate direction. And they gave that as westerly in the direction, as you have just mentioned, as indeed this report on the screen here says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In various documents produced by the CSB, there are different values for this bearing. In the document that you see in front of you on the screen, the CSB ballistic expert established, and you can see that beneath this figure of 120 centimetres that we mentioned, they claim that the shell fell on Klara Cetkin Street in front of number 4 came slightly to the north with respect to the west.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is in contravention of the finding that it had come from the westerly direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I don't know if I'm reading it the same as him. I see that the report says: Most clearly visible in a westerly direction, i.e., north in relation to the true west. Is that what Mr. Lukic is referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether this is not precisely the west; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just be enlightened, Mr. Lukic. What does northerly direction in relation to the west mean, and how does that become west? I'm asking Mr. Higgs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I read on this report says that the fire came from a slightly northerly direction in relation to the west. I don't understand that phrase myself. Now, Mr. Lukic says, suggests to you, that is that not west. And you agree with him that it is west. And I said: What does this phrase mean and how does this phrase equal west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in way this report has been written is what they mean is the general direction was to the west, but for this particular round it has come in a few degrees just to the north of west. And, again, they're approximating because obviously the poor quality of the craters in this case. So I read it to read that probably just slightly north of where true west would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And slightly north of where west could be, then that becomes west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it's in that general westerly direction, but probably just a few degrees probably north of west is what they are suggesting here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, as for the firing position, the report indicates Nedzarici or, rather, the institution for visually impaired persons. Do you know what is the bearing between the institute and the point of impact on Klara Cetkin Street number 4?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we -- or can we agree that 200 degrees equals west, with regard to the north; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 270 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] 180 plus 90.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. West would be 270 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Captain Verdy -- can we look at RN 10570, whilst in fact we have heard that it has already become an exhibit, D178. Captain Verdy found that the bearing of one shell was 4200 mills. Between 4200 and 4250 even. This is actually 236 degrees. We are talking about the southwesterly direction. Did you manage to establish where this difference of over 30 degrees may have come from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not possible because I could not do a detailed investigation, but from looking at the -- the forensic report, which is far more detailed, then I am a little bit suspicious that Captain Verdy has -- can be such a precise angle of approach when we know that the craters were not of a good quality. So I don't know how he has come to these readings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the same quality of the crater was found by the members of the CSB who carried out the investigation. The quality of the traces was the same for them, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it should have been. If I remember correctly, the forensic investigation was carried out on the day, and this one, I believe, was the following day, so they should have had similar crater information to work from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D667.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a photo which depicts a view from the institute for the blind to the place of the incident behind the buildings that we will see in the photo. Do you remember that if you were there, that the place of the incident was sheltered or obstructed from view by these buildings; i.e., you didn't have a clear sight from the institute for the blind towards the place of the incident because of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a compound question. There's many submissions in there too. I believe it would be just prudent to go step by step and just know whether or not the witness is, one, familiar with this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness is free to answer whatever he wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's one question taken altogether; that is, whether the view was obstructed. That is what we are talking about. Could the witness answer the question if he is able to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember if this is the view of the area that I would have seen at the time. I can't remember if this is the same place or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there was a line of view between the point of impact and the institute for the blind? If you don't remember, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let's focus on the incident that happened in Dobrinja on the 1st of June, 1993. We're talking about a football game, of course. Did I understand you properly when you said that you didn't take any measurements? You did not measure the distance between the craters, you didn't take the bearings or any such thing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took approximate bearings of the craters that were there at the time, although they were not good quality, but did not take any of the measurements to the buildings, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were there, the area was still the same. Nothing had been reconstructed; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of whether anything had or had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you still see the traces of the explosions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was two craters in the ground which had been filled with some form of red substance that I was taken to and shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the shells had fallen in relation to the football pitch; i.e., the place where the football game was taking place at the time? Did somebody show that place to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not where the football pitch was. It was commented in -- in -- in the reports where they thought they had landed, but I wasn't shown it physically on -- on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those people who manned the Serbian position could not see the place where the football game was taking place due to the fact that that place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Serb position refers to what? There are many areas where -- which were under Serb control. So, therefore, it's difficult to understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me rephrase the question. Thank you. I'll try and be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the football pitch in question is surrounded by eight-storey buildings from three sides, and those buildings completely sheltered the football pitch from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. The only open side faced the Mojmilo hilltop, which at the time was under the control of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's many questions in one. Could we first ask about the buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to my recollection there are buildings on three sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not on the fourth side. May I take it that there's no dispute between the parties about which was the open side and which were the built-up sides? We've seen photographs many, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell us how did you establish that you had arrived at the place where UNPROFOR had been on the day of the incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigators took me to the site, showed me the craters in the ground, then showed me where that was in relation to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up 1D1398.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this report drafted by UNPROFOR, which is actually a crater analysis, UNPROFOR also determined the co-ordinates. And we can see what the co-ordinates are. On page 1, it says what the crater's position was for both crater 1 and crater 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, I have this exhibit admitted -- or this document admitted as part of P644, e-court page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you check the co-ordinates in question? Did you do it when you were there at the scene?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I checked the approximate co-ordinates. It's one grid reference given, so it won't be a grid reference of the precise craters because there's only one grid reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D1399, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have plotted the co-ordinates on the map of Sarajevo and we can see that this is actually outside of the neighbourhood in question. Is this what you established? And what you established, does it correspond to our depiction on the map, or, alternatively, did you find something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the use of this diagram. I see in the UNPROFOR report that -- that was just used that the scale of map used to determine the grid reference was 1:50.000 and this looks like it comes from our map book which is a different scale. And based on that, the grid references might be in place in different locations. I ask that [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Weber, Mr. Weber, are you really telling us that grid references change with the scale of the map? Is that seriously your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on the scale, and I see the one attached to it and I've compared these two, slight, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Grid references are absolute. They have got nothing to do with a scale of a map, I would say, but if we would have a map with a sufficient precise scale, we could check it easily. I cannot understand that the parties, if there's such an issue, Mr. Lukic, that you have not discussed it with the Prosecution because if you're right, the Prosecution would have to -- perhaps to reconsider its position. Therefore, these are absolute numbers, apart from that it's always an area, depending on the -- how many digits we have in the grid references. So, therefore, a small square indicating where it is, you should be able to agree on that. And another matter is, is this the only grid references in any reports on the matter, or are there others? The Chamber would be interested to know if all the grid references mentioned in reports give a different location compared to what we see in the photographs. So, therefore, -- but, of course, the -- I take it that the witness is unable to say anything about it until -- unless provided with a clear map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. To have a more accurate estimate of these grid references, we really need to use ideally the map that was used by the investigators, the same type of map and also the map series number because they do sometimes slightly differ depending what map was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not dependant on the scale, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. As long as you are using the same map series, then the scale is immaterial. Obviously the bigger the scale, the more accurate you can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Lukic, this map on which you plotted the grid reference, where do we find -- is -- is this the -- the lines on it, are these the exact grid lines or -- because this seems to be -- not to be taken from a military map but, rather, from a civilian map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose it's civilian map, yes. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And have you checked whether there's any difference between the maps, or military maps, which would ordinarily be used by military people?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were here to testify maybe I would be obliged to answer. I asked this witness, has he checked. If he hasn't, that's fine with us. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the first question is: Did you ever consult this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I used the map that was in the -- in the report, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you check the UNPROFOR's claims? Did you try to establish whether the grid reference points that they had established were actually correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Using the map on the -- the report, which is a lot smaller scale, it indicated the -- the general area where these rounds are -- landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you able to establish whether there is a correspondence, or could you not establish that, or did you establish that the two did not correspond to each other?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They don't correspond exactly, no. It -- it -- it is in the same general area, but I would not say the grid reference is pin-point accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let's just go back briefly to 1D1398.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, or perhaps we should wait for the document to appear, that, according to UNPROFOR, those rounds had landed on a macadam surface?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what was reported here, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can also see that they noted two directions: One of 143 degrees, and the other of 138 degrees. If this were correct, would that mean that the rounds did not come from the same place, that they didn't originate from the same -- same place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It would depend how far away the mortar could be, 138 and 143, it's only a 5-degree difference, and the two rounds did not land in exactly the same place. So depending how far away the mortar was, which we don't know, one bout could have fired these two. But just as easily it could have been fired by two separate mortars as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, Witness, on the basis of a pattern of impact or, as it said here, splinter pattern, what would be the margin of error in establishing the direction of the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With good craters, at least plus or minus 5 degrees, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know, don't you, that the CSB Sarajevo carried out an investigation on the 21st November 1995 at the request of the Prosecutor's office of the ICTY; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not aware of an investigation in 1995. It was not one I used as part of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at P872, page 3 in English as well as in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we have before us is a record of forensic investigation of the scene of a shelling attack at a parking lot in 36 Dobrinja neighbourhood where it says: "On 20 November 1995 an investigator of the International Criminal Tribunal in The Hague, Jan van Hecke, conducted an interview with Zlatko Medjedovic in RBiH MUP offices. On this occasion, Mr. Jan van Hecke delivered Zlatko Medjedovic a request for a forensic investigation of the scene of a shelling attack and we can see that the incident happened on the 1st of June, 1993, because it is claimed that at the time of the incident a forensic investigation was not carried out due to incessant attack operations." And now I would like to look at page 5 in English and page 4 in B/C/S. In the last paragraph on this page, it says: "The point of impact of the second shell was not forensically examined due to the changed appearance of the soil adjacent to the parking lot ..." Would you be able to explain how you managed to find the traces of the second shell a few years later when even those investigators couldn't do it before you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean that reference to "those investigators couldn't do it"? Is that related to what is reported that the ongoing operations would not allow to do that investigation? Is that a reference to that, Mr. -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1995, they found only one trace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And where do we find that? I'm just -- you read --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly in this paragraph. It says: Second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The point of impact of the second shell was not forensically examined due to the altered appearance of the place of impact and the soil adjacent to the parking lot (various agricultural plants have been planted there in the meantime). A photo file was created during the making of this record."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not -- what confused me, as a matter of fact, is that you read that the investigation could not take place and the day [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- after that you have not read that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas the report says that what was not possible on the -- I think it was the 20th of November, that that investigation took place on the 21st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 21st of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The investigation was not -- performed on June 1st, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the first paragraph on -- if we can move back, it's page 3 in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I read is that - and that's what you read - is that on the -- let me see. Oh, that date is the 1st of June, yes. And then the investigation took place not on the 20th but on the 21st of November, 1995. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was this: How do you account for the fact that when you inspected the place of the incident a few years after 1995, you found two craters there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not obviously aware that in this investigation if they were even looking at the same craters that I did, but when I was taken to the location, there were two craters clearly marked, both filled in with this red substance which I have mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, were you told when those craters that you found there were created?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the craters were created; i.e., when the explosions took place? And I'm talking about the craters that you inspected. Did anybody expressly tell you the craters were created at that specific point in time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the investigator took me to the scene. They directed me to those two craters and informed me that these were the two craters used in this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can't ask you whether you compared the craters because you have just told us that you were not even aware of this report that we have before us at the moment.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can go back to 1D1398.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know that UNPROFOR did not determine the angle of descent because there was no fuse furrow. We will see that when the document appears and the -- both are valid for -- and -- and that -- that information is valid for both crater 1 and crater 2.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. No -- no measurement of the angle of descent was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The angle of descent was determined based on the height of the buildings, as you can see in paragraph 1; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He based it on a minimum that would have been required to clear the buildings, and then from the -- the general pattern on the ground has come up with quite a -- a wide span of which the rounds could have come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. Under item 2, there is nothing specific relating to the incident. They just copied data from the firing table that the smallest --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please give us figures slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, you are again invited to give numbers slowly. But perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in point 2 in this document, what I'm reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that doesn't change the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I used the time for the following: The Chamber will now turn to a matter related to its decision on the Prosecution's first intercept bar table motion. On the 2nd of May of this year, the Chamber issued its decision on the Prosecution's bar table motion for the admission of intercepts related to the Srebrenica segment of its case. On the 3rd of October, the Prosecution indicated by way of informal communication that it had complied with the Chamber's instructions concerning the uploading of particular documents related to this decision, with the exception of further identifying those that could be made public. As of today, the Chamber has not received such additional information and, therefore, the Chamber asks the Prosecution when it intends to comply with this instruction. Furthermore, the Chamber additionally instructs the Prosecution to provide by way of a filing the reasons that the remaining intercepts should retain their confidential status. And before we finally take the break, I would like to briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We take a break, and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom, I would briefly address the following matter: The Chamber turns to a matter related to -- let me see. I am afraid I have the wrong copy before me. I refrain from doing it at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read again from the document that we have before us, 1D1398, where, under item 2, it says: "The minimum angle of descent for 81-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortars is 45.71 degrees. At that angle, the minimum range is 1120 metres for 81-millimetre mortar, and 1340 metres for 120-millimetres mortar." Mr. Higgs, would you agree that this is a theory rather than the practice. This information has nothing to do with what was actually measured on the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This is just showing what sort of ranges could be achieved if the mortars fired on their lowest angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, with the lowest charge? Or is it on any specific charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With those ranges, Your Honour, it would be on their lowest charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once again, before we move to the next document, let's focus on the degrees in this document: 143 degrees for crater 1; and 138 degrees for crater 2. Now, let us look at document P872, please. As you can see, this is a file produced as a result of an on-site investigation carried out on the 21st November, 1995, relating to the Dobrinja incident which took place on the 1st of June, 1993. We need 5 -- page 5 in English and page 4 in the B/C/S version. Regarding this incident, the investigators of the Sarajevo police department, whilst they were working together with the ICTY Prosecutor's office, established that, as it is written here: "With the use of the plan of the Dobrinja neighbourhood and a compass, we determined the angular span between the northerly directions and the direction of the incoming artillery shell in relation to the centre of the explosion, which equals 110 degrees from the north." This differs from what was established by UNPROFOR yet again. This is at variance with the allegations of UNPROFOR that the angle was 140, actually 143 and 138 degrees respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is the question, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this is different for more than 35 degrees -- or, I'm sorry, 25 degrees, in excess of 25 degrees if compared to the UNPROFOR findings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this report does give a different bearing. But it must be remembered that this is taken possibly two years later, and with degradation of the area not surprising it would come up with a slightly different reading, if that is the case here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The point Mr. Lukic is making is it's not slightly, but it's considerable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that UNPROFOR had determined the direction from which the shell came in their report without determining the type of the shell or the descent angle of the shell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the -- the type, they did remark that it was of medium calibre: 81 millimetre or 82 millimetre. But they did not work out angle of descent or the range. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is not sufficient information in order to determine the position from which the shell was fired?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct, as you only have the bearings and nothing to give an indication of -- of the range in which the weapon was fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 9939, please. It's a document which was partially adopted as P644 but not in its entirety, and we are going to use it as indicated. Let's look at page 5 in English and page 4 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that UNPROFOR investigators who investigated this incident in June and July of 1993 never visited the scene, in actual fact? One can see that from item 7.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that from the item 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says that UNPROFOR officials indicated that the area is exposed to small-arms fire and therefore dangerous. Would you agree with me that due to the position of buildings or -- could we say that this area was secluded from three sides by eight-storey buildings; therefore, there was no danger coming from small-arms fire from the Serbian positions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's impossible for me to give a detailed answer on that, because they obviously believed from reading this report that it is coming under fire. I've got no evidence to contradict that, so I can't give an accurate response.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to put on the record I know counsel is directing him to page 7, but I believe counsel's representation was that UNPROFOR never visited the scene. I don't read the report as a broad a scope as never. I agree that paragraph 7 says what it says, on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, this report has never been finished because [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that's a -- that's a different matter, Mr. -- you can still go to the scene and not finish the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, I'm more interested in the relationship between the Sarajevo authorities and UNPROFOR and what kind of assistance it was provided at the time. It says here, under item 8, the author of the report says: "I asked Mr. Kosavec if there were any documents or photographs, relating to this incident that would be available to assist in our enquires. He stated that any documents of that nature would be held by the chief of police of Dobrinja, and requested we attend the Dobrinja police station on the morning of the 2nd July 1993." Then it goes on. Under item 9, it says: "At approximately 0907 hours on the 2nd of July, 1993, accompanied by Sergeant Lamothe and other members of the war crimes investigation team, I attended the Dobrinja police station where we met with Mr. Kosavec and the chief of police. We were advised that all investigative material relating to this incident had been forwarded to the main police station in Sarajevo. "When he went to the police station, Mr. Mochibob was informed that the materials relating to this shelling incident were currently not available but could be fetched on the 2nd of July at 1400 hours from the main police station." So item 11, the 2nd of July, we need page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Slow down. Slow down. Slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 5 in B/C/S. So item 11 - I'm not going to read the whole of it: "They went where they had been told to go," and I'm not going to read the whole paragraph, "and they were told that they had nothing and that it might have been investigated by the Bosnian army. He said that UNPROFOR attributed this incident to the Serbian army and that as far as that went, that was sufficient for him." Then, again, in paragraph 14 -- so my question for you is this: Is it true that UNPROFOR official never received the relevant documents from the police relating to that particular investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't -- I don't know because I'm not a member of the UNPROFOR so I don't know whether they did or did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just going to invite Mr. Lukic to look at paragraph 12 which might just give a slightly different answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we have to go back to the previous page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's only on weather condition, Your Honour, not on the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It says that, "He provided us with the records for the 1st of June, 1993." Whatever those records might be, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Says: "He provided with us with the records for the 1st June, 1993, which showed the visibility at the time of the incident was 10 kilometres with calm winds."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does this report have Annex H to it and what does Annex H --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This report has many annexes, I think. It is divided in several parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Higgs, let us look at item 14: "On 4th of July, 1993, at approximately 0945 I received a copy of a map of Dobrinja from UNPROFOR officials, a copy of which is attached as Annex I. This map shows that the soccer game was held in a location surrounded on three sides by buildings (west, east, and south). In addition, it was explained that there are Bosnian mortars located outside the hospital approximately 500 metres from the soccer location. However, these were not observed during our visit to the Dobrinja area." In your report, did you explore the possibility of a mortar belonging to the BH Army being deployed in the vicinity of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this report. I have not done any investigation to prove where these mortars actually were around the hospital, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The hospital. Which hospital did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the investigators took me to this site, they showed me the area of -- where the hospital is. I'm assuming this is the same one that is being related to here. I have got no grid references or facts. So I was taken to a site, at least they told me it was a hospital, but, of course, it was on that visit impossible to know where the mortars may or may not have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just to check whether you're talking about the same hospital. In your question, "the hospital," which hospital and where located did you understand the reference relates to? Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understood that it was 500 metres from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The place of impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that gives a circle with some thousand positions for hospitals, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think that in Dobrinja you have more than one hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Which one? Where is that located because that is my -- where did you understand it was located when you put the question to the witness and when you read the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter -- it's on our screen. We just need e-court page 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see there an indication of hospital, "hopital," to the left. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes. Actually, it has to be, I think -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where it has to be, that's where it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... counter-clockwise, although it's written here in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at this moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is hospital, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I was trying to avoid because gentleman told us yesterday that he is not privy with the area so I was -- but if you want, we can -- we can discuss it with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The only thing is that if you put a question about "the hospital," I'd like to know where it is. Because if you invite the witness to explore whether that was -- and I understood that to be the gist of your question, whether he had considered the possibility that it was fired from there, then for the Chamber it's important to know where that would have been so that, at least the Chamber, in the totality of the evidence, can consider whether that is an option, yes or no. And for that reason, we have to know what hospital you referred to in the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you find your bearings in this map? And with relation to the hospital, can you mark the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am looking at the diagram correctly, I believe the incident would be in this area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] One of the shell, yes, in that area.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And [Interpretation] Here, you can see the words "police" in this map. Did you establish whether any shell fell in that area on that same day? And that the street that we mentioned earlier, Dzavarahalal Nehura Street?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not look into any other rounds fired on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Perhaps -- but can you please just put the number 1 where the hospital is, although there is some markings in the map already.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You put number 1, indicating where the hospital is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And after this, we would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D408, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.text: Yes. And then we briefly stopped where we stopped now, and then you indicate when we would move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop. At 12:33 video time, we moved to 13 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 12:23, it seems to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. 12:23, video time. We moved to 13 hours camera time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Higgs, we have seen that at 1245 camera time, a shot was taken of a mortar stabiliser at this same location without any number. utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if -- well, how, it could have been moved. I can only go from the damage that I can see on the -- the pictures of the stabiliser, where it appears to be -- the damage is consistent in both pictures, so I don't know if it was moved or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may Your Honour, this witness said that he saw this video before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But before he wasn't able to see whether someone moved it either. He just doesn't know. That's what he tells us. The only thing he knows is that what he sees is damage of such similarity on two stills that he thinks that it's the same tail-fin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]
