utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, today I'm going to attempt to clarify some matters with respect to the type of shells that had been discussed during your testimony. On Tuesday, at pages 18840 to 18857, you were shown firing tables and trajectories for an M49 P1 (OF-843/1) shell fired from an M74 mortar. Do you recall being shown this material and being asked to mark on portions of it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P498, page 20 of the B/C/S original, and page 17 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: While this is coming up, I'm going to be starting with the BiH MUP police ballistics analysis for Markale II. I'm going to then, from this, ask you to walk us through some materials today and then afterwards I will have more detailed questions about the certain type of mortar shells and tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could please have the lower portion of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to findings number 4 and 5 on this page, could you please tell us what type of shell fragments were found at the scene of the Markale II shelling.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From section -- sorry, paragraph 4, it states that parts belonging to the front curve part of a 120-millimetre light fuse contact high explosive-type shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And does finding number 5 also correspond to a 120-millimetre light fuse contact high explosive-type shell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to directing your attention now up to findings number 2 and 3 on the same page. Could you please tell us what type of fuse the BiH concluded was used?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, they state that it belonged -- type of fuse belonging to an M62 designed for mortar projectile 120-millimetre, and in sub-para 3, again, it says M62 type fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to clarify this because the similarity in numbers. So I just wanted you to see this. We're now going to move to the JNA operations manual regarding 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30261, page 159 of the B/C/S and page 119 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, the page that's coming up before you is from the operation manual for the M74 and M75 mortars. Directing your attention to section number 4, regarding the M62 UTU impact fuse with instantaneous and delayed action, is this the same type of fuse that the BiH police found at the location of the Markale II shelling?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has the same designation number as the report we've just seen, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the first sentence of paragraph 385, could you please tell us the type of shell that an M62 UTU impact fuse is intended for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The impact fuse is instantaneous and delayed actions intended for an M62 light contact-fuse shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's go to that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the same manual, could the Prosecution please have page 142 of the B/C/S and page 106 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to number 6 for the M62 120-millimetre light contact-fuse shell, can you just confirm that this is the same type of shell that the M62 UTU fuse that we just looked at was intended for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked the attention for -- to number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 6 of what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it's right before paragraph 346.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was transcribed as number 6. And that's how you understood. 346, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this type of light contact-fuse shell consistent with the type of shell fragments that the BiH police investigators found at the location of the Markale II shelling?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 18908 of yesterday's transcript, you stated that the analysis of distances you performed for Markale II was based on the M62 shell. Is it correct that you used the firing tables corresponding to this type of light contact-fuse shell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now could the Prosecution please go to page 140 of the B/C/S and page 105 of the English translation of the manual. And, Your Honours, I'm going to be focussing on the part right above paragraph 343.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For completeness, I'd like to address with you the M49 P1 with parenthetical designations of (OF-943) and (843/1). At the heading on this page it says it's a 120-millimetre modified contact-fuse shell. If you could please look at paragraph 343, is it correct that these shells can also be used with the M62 UTU fuses?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it states on line 3 that B-45 fuses were replaced with new M62 fuses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, this is described as a modified shell according to the heading. Before moving on, I'd like to draw your attention to the first sentence of the paragraph numbered 343 which states: "These are, in fact, modified shells described in paragraphs 335-342." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 137 of the B/C/S and page 103 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the heading of section number 2 on this page, which is right above paragraph number 335, these following paragraphs relate to an OF-843 heavy contact-fuse shell. Could you please review this page and let me know when we can move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S version, the next page continues through to the next two pages, in the B/C/S. So if we could please have the next page of the English translation. I just want to note for the record that it carries over for two pages in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, could you please let me know when you've completed your review of this page.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for reviewing those pages. Do I correctly understand that a MP49 P1 shell is a type of heavy contact-fuse shell, according to the paragraphs you just reviewed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We will look at some specific data in a second. But, first, I would like to simply ask you whether a heavy contact-fuse shell is different than the light contact-fuse shell found near the Markale market by the BiH police investigators.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From reading the text here is that the thickness of the wall is different between the two rounds, so the two rounds do have different characteristics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please now go to 65 ter 30458, page 2. This is an uploaded excerpt of Defence 65 ter 1D1293, page 16. And in the B/C/S version, if we could please rotate clockwise 90 degrees the page and then focus on the top half.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, I'm going to be directing your attention to the chart on this page that its head is: M74 mortar ammunition basic data. Will you please let me know if you can locate the appropriate numbers corresponding to the M49 P1 series and also the M62 series?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it possible to blow it up, make it a bit bigger, so that I can see the data? The top three lines relate to M49. And then the -- we then have a different types of M62s then at different lines further down the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And based on the data, could you please explain to us what the significant difference is between an M49-type shell and an M62-type shell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the main differences was explained in the previous document, where the M49 has a thicker wall jacket to the explosive part of the round.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the shell mass without the fuse. If -- you can let me know whether or not there's a -- I view it that there's -- that the M49 series weighs 15.780 kilograms. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the M62 series varies a little, but it weighs 12.1 grams [sic] with the M62 being 12.160, and the M62 P3 being slightly lighter. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You wanted to refer to kilograms, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would the difference in weight between -- or what -- what would be the significance of the difference in weight between these two types of series in terms of it -- the velocity of these shells, the height that they would achieve, and the distance that they would travel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The M49, for its extra weight, it would affect its maximum range that it could achieve would be less; the vertex height it achieve would also be less; and its velocities would be low as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could I ask one additional question. Is this a conclusion on basis of the weight or is it also considering whether or not the charges, the propelling charges which are used to fire it are the same or different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be taking comparable charges, Your Honour, so a charge 2 on an M49 as opposed to a charge 2 on an M62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, would you use the same propelling charges for two such different kinds of shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the charges on the M49. They could be the same, but normally different types of ammunition would possibly have different types of charge systems as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, any conclusion as, because they are heavier they would travel slower with a shorter range is, if, as you said, is not usual if fired with the same propelling charges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, therefore, then I think the answer should have been it depends on whether the propelling charges are specific ones for those heavier shells or whether they are fired, which is quite unusual, with the same charges. Is that the full answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just on His Honour's question, directing your attention now over to the right column, do I read correctly that certain types of M49 shells can be used with the same type of additional charges as the M62 series shells, depending on its type?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we first ask whether the table contains any information as to the propelling charges being used with those?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, did you just hear His Honour's question or would you like me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this table give any information about the propelling charges to be used with this various kinds of shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the column second to the right, Your Honour, it gives a standard mark and then an additional one that can also be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they are different for the first three compared to lines 4 and 5, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, the charges --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't read line 5 as being different. I see your -- that line [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First standard, M67 - I only read the first part - second standard, M67; third standard, M67; fourth standard, M57; and then the fifth standard, M74. And then the additional charges for 1, 2, 3, and 5, seem to be the same; whereas, for line 4, it seems to be a different one, the additional charge is M56.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's how I read it too. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So standard different for the M62s. Additional charges different for one of the two M62s and the same as for the M49 for the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The last question I have on this chart is that since certain types of M49s -- let me rephrase this. If an M49 series type shell, heavy contact shell, was using the same type of fuse, an M62 UTU, as an M62 light contact shell with the type of fuse make any type of difference in the flight of a mortar round?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No discernible difference. The type of fuse wouldn't have a massive impact on the range, no, or the flight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that even be true if the weight of the fuse would be considerably different from the other ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that was the case, Your Honour, I have no evidence to prove that, but fuses are normally very similar types of weights on this type of round. But, yes, if -- if you did have a fuse which was noticeably heavier, then, yes, it would have an impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we see on line 5 a fuse with the weight which is approximately four times the weight of the other ones? 470 instead of 120.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you consider that to be a considerable difference in weight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. With this type of fuse that would make a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since we've gone through these materials, I'd just like to confirm with you that the firing tables that you were shown by the Defence for M49 P1, whether or not you can say those were the correct or incorrect firing tables for the type of charge that was found at -- or type of shell that was found at the Markale II scene which indicated it was a light contact-fuse?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were the wrong range tables, as the round -- parts of the round discovered at that scene were M62.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to move on, Your Honours, but I know that this was some technical material, so I just wanted to pause to see if you had any further questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, where are the applicable fire tables?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're -- I believe that they should all be tendered and in front of the Chamber, and I'm -- I think that we can agree to admit both the ones that apply to the M49 P1s and also the M62 series, and the Chamber will have the data translated in front -- in front of it to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do I understand that you would agree on providing tables for different types of shells --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and then we'll see what the difference in outcome is? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, during cross-examination, you were asked questions about possible locations where mortar fire can originate from. In particular, you were asked about the area around Mount Trebevic on transcript page 18815. I just have a more general question: What would make a particular location suitable for the firing of a mortar?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When positioning in a mortar, first of all, is -- taking into consideration is their own protection, so you would not want to put it too close in an exposed position to obviously enemy fire. So a protected location. Also keeping it as close as you can to a confrontation lines, you're getting maximum effect for the ranges of the charges that a mortar could fire. An example would be if you put -- placing your mortar so far to the rear where they have to fire at charge 6 at everything, then that may well be okay for a target which is directly in front of them, but if they're then called to engage a target which is further to the left or the right or further away, they probably won't be able to reach it. So you want your mortars to be close enough where they can use a full range of charge effectively but not that close where they put themselves in jeopardy from direct fire weapons from the opposing forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are there any physical characteristics of the ground or immediate area that would be preferable or make a certain specific location better for the firing of a mortar?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the other advantages which we have already discussed is altitude, so if you can get your mortars above the target locations, that will effectively increase your ranges for every charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you intend to ask about surface needed, flat or not, why not ask the witness because it seems that that's what you're [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is. I just didn't want to lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness express himself on what kind of terrain you would need not for tactical purposes but for technical purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Type of ground. You can fire mortars, really, from any type of ground. Obviously steep slopes cause an issue because the mortar needs to have predominantly a flatter surface to sit upon, which, of course, can be dug out. But if you can find ground which is predominantly flat, it makes the preparation area simpler to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many square metres would you need for the mortar itself, not for the crew yet but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For 120-millimetre mortar possibly 4 square metres of flight ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your previous testimony, you've discussed your experience with mortar investigations. I'd just like to, based on cross, ask you generally, when is the best time to -- to conduct a crater analysis as part of a mortar investigation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as possible after the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain why that is the case.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The quicker you can get to the location, obviously less degradation of the crater as there will be flash marks on the ground which could possibly be worn away with weather conditions. So the sooner you can get there and see it in its fresh state, the more accurate you can be with your findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And in the investigative materials that you reviewed for your report, did you rely on the materials that were done as close in time to when the shelling occurred?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain why you did that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because for the reasons just mentioned. The area -- sorry, the time as close as possible to when the incident took place, those investigations tend to be more accurate than if one was conducted at some time at later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the ground which the shell impacts is very hard, concrete or tarmac, would the difference in time be similarly important or would it be less important?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably less important as far as some of the major scrapes that may be affecting the road, but you would still lose any of the blast indications because they're obviously reliant on the weather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you exactly understand by blast indications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You may have a scorch marks which you could use on the ground, and, of course, they would not last as long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other blast marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the ones that would be worn away by the weather. The other ones caused by the shrapnel, of course, on hard ground would stay there a lot -- a lengthier time as opposed to, as you said, soft ground where it would degrade far quicker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was it at any time that you relied upon -- on these blast marks, as you just described them to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in this -- as I could -- because I was using obviously the data from other forces could not, from the photographs supplied, really use those in any -- enough detail to see any of those marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Scorch marks were considered by you in photographs or did you take them into consideration in any specific way? Were they reported at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not as reported at the time. No, I didn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the whole scorch marks is -- is not used either by you, or you found them in the earlier reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see specifically mentioned in the reports, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, the difference of immediately investigating and later looking at it, does not materialise in these reports and in your findings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see anything specifically related to it. I don't know if the teams on the ground used anything on calculating their bearings or not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could just have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll now move onto another topic. On Monday at transcript pages 18776 to 18787 and Tuesday at transcript pages 18800 to 18809, you were asked questions related to annotated photographs from your past Karadzic report and your current Mladic case report which depict different angles for the street where the Markale II shell landed. In a question about these annotated photos at transcript page 18801, you stated with respect to your determination of the direction of fire that: "My conclusion didn't change. My conclusion is still that the round has come from a direction closely around 170 degrees." Also at transcript page 18806, you stated in relation to these photographs that: "I am not carrying out a direct crater analysis." I'm sorry, your quote was: "I'm not carrying out here a direct crater analysis." Do you recall the annotated photographs that I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was assumed in these questions that you were performing a mathematical calculation of the direction of fire based on the direction of the street. I have the following question: Does whatever angle the street runs along have any effect on the measurement of the mortar crater to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the investigation teams would not have used that in their investigation. They would have taken it from the pattern of the crater on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have -- excuse me, before moving on to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This morning in relation to incident G4, the football match, Mr. Lukic asked you about the visibility of the soccer pitch from VRS positions. Can I ask you: Is it necessary, or even common, for the soldier actually manning the mortar to have visibility of the intended target?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just seek some verification. Mr. Lukic, when you put the question to the witness, was it -- was it about small-arms fire or was it about mortars? Visibility from Serb positions to -- or both?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This morning I was talking about small-arms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Small-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P538 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I'm -- I'm recapitulating what I was talking about. At the end I was talking about small-arms, but before, at the beginning of the day, I think I was talking about the mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why I asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... there was no visibility, according to our Defence, so you can apply it to any fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's why I asked: Or both.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think this morning, in total, both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see it is the possible time for a break. If I could break here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We can take a break. How much time would you still need after the break, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have actually just one section left. I have gone quicker than I expected. And then I do have a number of housekeeping items that I was hoping to at least address and resolve with the witness concerning the admission of the report and previous testimony and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what does that mean in minutes for the -- for the examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I probably will be another, at most, seven to eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then there will still be some time left, Mr. Lukic, if there is any need for further cross. Could the witness follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While the witness is brought in ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, your last seven to eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P538, page 20 of the original, which is written in French, and page 28 of the B/C/S translation. Since this document is not in the witness's native language the Prosecution has brought clean copies of the English translation for the witness and anyone else who would like a copy of the English translation. The Prosecution has uploaded the English translation under 65 ter 100 -- I'm sorry, 10010B, as in boy. We'll be asking that this be included with the exhibit at the conclusion of the examination. If I could ask the Court Officer to please hand the witness a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it there's no objection against attaching the English translation to the French original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then leave is granted to attach to P538, the English translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, yesterday you were asked a number of questions about the covers related to the Markale I shelling in February 1994. Before you is UNPROFOR Staff-Sergeant Dubant's report related to his examination of the crater at the Sarajevo market. I was wondering if you could please review this document and let us know when you're complete with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, just in case you're interested, in the pages following in this report, in the uploaded version of P538, the sketches are present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've read that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Higgs, I just wanted to give you the time to read the full report but what I'm going to focus on with you relates to the second paragraph from the top, in particular, the portion that starts: "I could see that the lateral spray which was clean and sharp had been produced by direct impact on the ground. We were able to rule out the possibility that the mortar shell had hit one of the market stalls before hitting the ground." He then lists three points that led him to this conclusion. In reviewing these three-points, do you agree that these are consistent with Staff-Sergeant Dubant's conclusion that the mortar made a direct impact upon the ground?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From seeing of the -- the photographs, the videos, and from looking at the points here that this gentleman has made, yes, I would concur that the round detonated when it hit the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's all I have for re-examination. At this time I would re-tender a number of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we move to that, Mr. Lukic, have the cross-examination [sic] has it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just have a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we first deal with that, Mr. Weber, if you would not mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Just so I don't lose track of it, there were a -- manual that -- there were two different -- I used the JNA manual and also the excerpt. We will further discuss that with the Defence, and then also if the Chamber has any preference on what sections that they would see -- seek or like, we're happy to also include those. They are available under the 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, again, you would prefer to first discuss the matter with Mr. Lukic and then to make a joint -- or at least that Mr. Lukic can add whatever he thinks relevant before you tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's accepted. We will keep that in the back of our mind. Anything else, at this moment, Mr. Weber, before we move to a few other matters. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Higgs, just briefly. It has been suggested to you that Defence erroneously used M49 tables, that, instead, we should have used M62 tables. Would you agree with me that M62 has a longer trajectory and that the vertex point of the trajectory would be higher if compared to the trajectory of M49?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report on page 15, you have cited different ranges for charges 1, 2, 3, and 4. When you were drafting this, did you use any tables at all in order to determine the ranges?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the M62 tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the pages and the exhibits from which you extracted these data, and the tables as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the page numbers, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was also suggested to you today that it shouldn't have been taken into account at all, regarding incident Markale II, the angle of the street. Would you agree with me that when you were doing your measurements and calculations, you linked your findings to the curb of the street - that is on page 14 of your report - which, in fact, contains the direction of the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I used the angle of the street to give me an approximate direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Higgs. This is all that I wanted to ask you. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have one question. We looked at this French report a minute ago, the three reasons given why the impact would have been on the ground rather than to hit a stall. Now, I saw that that black marking is the black markings which I do understand to be scorch marks is mentioned here. Have you considered this report when preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen this before today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was only for the first time. Okay. Thank you. No further questions for you. Then do we need the presence of the witness to deal with the administrative matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not, I would like to thank you, Mr. Higgs, very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answering all the questions that were put to you, either by the parties or by the Bench, and we regret that we were not able to release you any earlier, but at least now you can travel home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I have a few matters. I think, in relation to D399, you raised that one before, that was the Google Earth map, which was marked for identification to give you some time to consider your position. You addressed that exhibit. Is there any position yet by the Defence, or is it a matter you'll further work out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you know, I'm not privy with the Sarajevo area, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then leave that for the time being. Then I move to D356, excerpts of the 82-millimetre mortar manual. D356 was MFI'd during the testimony of Witness Turkusic. And the Prosecution indicated in an informal communication that the parties discussed the tendering of additional excerpts but that it was still awaiting a translation. The Chamber wondered whether there's any update in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, correct. We made a selection of additional portions of that, some of which was not translated. Since it was our selections, we did put in translation request which we were told would be available in a month from the date of that communication. So at the point in time that -- as earlier as possible when those translations are available, if it's okay with the Chamber if we could address it and then seek admission at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The date of that communication being?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd have to look that up, that precise date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is that 28 days ago or was it yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which leaves still 26 days. I do understand that it was somewhere at the end of October. So, therefore, most likely another two and a half to three weeks to wait for. Then, finally, the witness's report. Unless there's anything to be said in addition at this very moment to what has been submitted already previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nothing -- nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have considered the parties' filings and we have heard the testimony of the witness, and the Chamber decides to admit the witness's report previously marked as P2605, as well as the witness's previous testimony marked as P2606 and P2607. In addition, the Registry is instructed to replace the current version of P2606 with the corrected version, which was uploaded under Rule 65 ter number 30277a. Is there ... have the parties any further matters? If not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you took care of most of my matters. The one other matter that I had is that we did prepare a table of concordance for both the items referenced in the report and also the items referenced in the previous testimony tendered pursuant to Rule 92 ter. This table is available under 65 ter 30453 and that we ask that it be admitted at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no objection, I take it. It's purely instrumental --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... instrumental and doesn't add anything. Mr. Registrar, the number for 65 ter 30453 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2628, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. I will briefly deal with one more matter, which is the Prosecution request for leave to reply to the Defence response to the military justice bar table motion. The Chamber recalls that on the 25th of October, the Prosecution requested an extension of seven days in which to file a request for leave to reply to the Defence response to the military justice bar table motion. This request was granted by the Chamber on the 28th of October, whereby the Chamber stated that the seven-day extension was running as of that day, the 28th of October, making the deadline the 4th of November. The request for leave to reply and the attached reply were filed on the 5th of November, 2013. The Chamber considers this filing to be: One, a request for leave to reply; and, second, a corrigendum to the motion withdrawing the tendering of four documents. Considering that the reply was filed on the 5th of November, the Chamber will, pursuant to Rule 126 bis, deny the requested leave to reply, as the filing was submitted after the expiration of the prescribed deadline. The Chamber will, however, consider the withdrawal of the tendering of four documents as indicated by the Prosecution in the request for leave to reply as a corrigendum. For the clarity of the record, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to specify which documents are subject to the withdrawal. It's time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may swiftly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. We just want to attach one English translation to one of the MFI'd documents. It's 1D1355, now D389, MFI'd. There is English translation under doc ID 1D06-0678.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, what was the document, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was D389.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No. What was the document about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just got this message from our Case Manager, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I will give you a similar message that we'll -- we'll grant leave to attach the English translation to the document MFI'd as D389. D389 is admitted into evidence and if there's any problem with the English translation or if there's any other reason for objections by the Prosecution, we'd like to hear not any later than by Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we adjourn for the day, and we'll resume Monday, the 11th of November, and if I'm not mistaken in this same Courtroom III, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of November, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
